LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard metadata variable definitions and array assignments at the top level. The `source` array declares a GitHub tarball URL using normal AUR syntax (`file::url`), and the `sha256sums` array provides a valid checksum. There are no top-level commands, variable assignments that execute code, or network operations during sourcing. The `::` syntax is standard AUR source formatting and does not trigger downloads when merely defining the variable. No `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, `wget`, or other suspicious constructs appear at the global scope. Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only parse and output source metadata without executing any build or fetch logic, as `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` are explicitly out of scope.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>PKGBUILD metadata parsing is safe</summary>
</security_assessment>
